title: Where Malware Protection and ATP checks fall in the web enforcement order

checks.do: Whether the transaction is a GET request, a POST request or a response, since each has its own order.
Which numbered step is the earliest one that could have fired, since the first violation blocks the transaction.

first-violation-blocks.statement: When the web module finds a transaction violates a policy, the Public Service Edge blocks it immediately and does not enforce the policies that follow; the firewall module does not evaluate it, though firewall logs still show the web transaction as blocked.

quotes: the Public Service Edge immediately blocks that transaction and does not continue enforcing the policies that follow.
However, your firewall logs show that the user's web transaction is blocked.

get-order.statement: For an HTTP GET request the order is: 1 Custom Malicious URLs (ATP denylist), 2 Cloud App Control, 3 URL Filtering, 4 Security Exceptions, 5 Browser Control, 6 Country-Based Blocking, 7 IPS Signature Detection, 8 Suspicious Content Protection (Page Risk), 9 P2P Control, 10 Bandwidth Control. Malware Protection and Sandbox are not in the GET request list.

evidence.after: This is a user request to retrieve a resource from the web (e.g., a web page).

get-order.conditions: The absence of Malware Protection from the GET list is read from the document's list; files in GET responses are covered by the response order.

post-order.statement: For an HTTP POST request the order is: 1 Custom Malicious URLs, 2 Cloud App Control, 3 URL Filtering, 4 Security Exceptions, 5 Browser Control, 6 Country-Based Blocking, 7 Malicious URL Block (the Zscaler URL database), 8 IPS Signature Detection, 9 Suspicious Content Protection, 10 Malware Protection, 11 File Type Control, 12 Data Loss Prevention, 13 P2P Controls, 14 Bandwidth Control.

evidence.after: This is a user request to submit or post data to the web

response-order.statement: For an HTTP response the order is: 1 Security Exceptions, 2 IPS Signature Detection, 3 Suspicious Content Protection, 4 Sandbox check for known malicious files, 5 Malware Protection, 6 File Type Control, 7 Sandbox analysis of unknown files, then AI/ML-based content categorization. The custom malicious URL list and country blocking are not in the response list.

evidence.after: This is data sent from the destination host back to the user in response to an HTTP GET

response-order.conditions: The absences are read from the document's response list.

mp-after-atp-checks.statement: In the POST request and in the response, the Malware Protection check comes after the ATP checks, so an ATP block ends the transaction before file scanning would run.
mp-after-atp-checks.conditions: Derived from the listed order and the stop-at-first-violation rule.
